Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
304 AM PST Sat Feb 21 2026

.SYNOPSIS...21/301 AM.

High pressure aloft building in over the region will bring a
warming trend into early next week. While temperatures will 
remain below normal today, temperatures above seasonal normals 
will develop by Sunday. A storm system will move into northern 
California during next week. Most of the area will likely remain 
dry. The highest chances of precipitation will be for San Luis 
Obispo County between Tuesday and Wednesday.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-MON)...21/301 AM.

Mostly clear skies prevail over the area this morning as ridging
aloft continues to build into the region. A cold air mass remains
in place over the area in the wake of the series of cold fronts. 
Clearer skies and lighter winds in place have made radiational 
cooling processes more efficient overnight and overnight low 
temperatures in wind-sheltered areas have plummeted to near or 
below freezing. Frost advisories already in place for the Ventura 
County valleys, the western San Fernando Valley, and the Santa 
Clarita Valley were expanded into the interior portions of the 
Santa Barbara portion of the Central Coast and the Santa Ynez 
Valley. Temperatures are sitting solidly in frost advisory 
criteria. In the Cuyama Valley, where a freeze warning is in 
effect, temperatures sit at or below the freezing mark.

Temperatures will start to warm today as the ridge aloft starts 
to modify the air mass. Temperatures will warm to just below 
normal today, then additional warming will take place through the
weekend. By Sunday, temperatures will warm above normal with high
temperatures in the mid 60s to mid 70s will be common for coastal
and valley locations. Except for some high clouds, skies will be 
mostly clear through the period.

.LONG TERM (TUE-FRI)...21/301 AM.

Across the forecast ensembles, good agreement exists through
Tuesday for a warming trend to persist. Temperatures will be well
above normal, touching the low 80s in some spots on Monday and 
Tuesday. The ridge will likely amplify due to the atmospheric 
river type storm system moving farther to the north and allow for 
a warmer air mass to develop. Rain chances from late Monday
through Wednesday will likely be limited to northern San Luis 
Obispo County as the atmospheric river sags south. EPS ensembles 
suggest a high chance of rain for K87Q, while GEFS and CMC 
ensembles lean drier. NBM values remain in the long term due to 
forecast uncertainty. While onshore flow will likely bring some 
cooling for Tuesday and Wednesday, there is a moderate to high of 
chance of a further warming trend develop for Thursday and Friday
with weak offshore flow. Winds look to remain on the weak side, 
except for some breezy northerly winds on Tuesday night and 
Wednesday night.

&&

.AVIATION...21/0725Z.

At 0630Z at KLAX, no inversion and no marine layer were present. 

High confidence in TAFs with VFR conditions and light winds 
through the period. 10% chance for VLIFR conds at KPRB after 10Z.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. There is a 10% chance of an
east wind component reaching 6 kt from 15Z-20Z Sat. 

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF.

&&

.MARINE...21/117 AM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current
forecast. Today there is a 40-60% chance of SCA level southerly 
winds in the late afternoon and overnight hours, highest across 
PZZ670. Moderate confidence in conditions remaining below SCA 
levels Sunday and Monday, then NW winds are expected to increase 
Tuesday.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate confidence in 
conditions remaining below SCA levels through Tuesday. 

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, high confidence in
conditions remaining below SCA levels through Tuesday.

&&
